originality.rationale: Full Section 4 of Antolini–Ballico–Oneto proves only nontransversality for general degree >=3 line-curve Hadamard surfaces; its conic example is a special cubic. Classical Polo-Blanco–van der Put–Top treats generic ruled quartic double curves and conductor but does not mark coordinate planes inherited from Hadamard multiplication. The precise 20 distinct nodes and 8 smooth tangencies versus 12 double-curve crossings, together with the Hadamard-specific determinant, are a stronger marked-boundary result, not a restatement of generic quartic classification. Related published-finding corpus hits concern a specific sharp quartic and two-conic Hadamard multiplication, neither implies the marked general line-conic assertion. Residual priority risk for unindexed boundary calculations remains.
residual_risks: An older or unindexed description of marked coordinate-plane intersections may exist.
